title: Switching to trumpet and buying Chicago buildings
summary: He changed horns, bought a Selmer secondhand, and recalls spending his earnings on flat buildings and lots that were later lost.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: I changed, I changed when I got here, didn't I? I was using the Wonder, wasn't I? Yeah. The Wonder was, Herbert L. Clark was his name. Oh, yeah, sure. It's in the Suzy's band. Yeah, he had the band, yeah. He made a horn that the tuning slide was in the back called a Wonder. You could hold it. And if it didn't suit your ears, all you had to do is touch it. Well, that was a cornet. Now, I changed to a Holton during the time I got a Holton, a brass Holton. I didn't keep that very long. But I bought two CG corn, cornets. I've never had a CG corn trumpet until I had this Selma. And after this horn was stolen from me, I had a chance to lock up on this horn cheap. And I bought it at a pawn shop down here on State in Van Buren. And just before you go, I'll show it to you. It keeps it locked up. Oh, yeah. Yeah, it keeps it locked up so you can. I don't leave it out. I'm just so afraid to keep it in the house almost, see. So, I haven't had my hands on it. But after we got here and played on and looked like I made, I guess it's like one of those things you make too much money and haven't got the schooling or the knowledge to do what you would like to do with those things. And nobody to help you and you start out with just money and no brains. I bought a flat building. And after I bought that building, I turned around and bought another building. Two flat buildings, 4914 Forestville and 450 East 50th Street. Then I bought 37 watts at 115th in May. That was just lots. Well, we lost all of that.
